name: APQC Process Classification Framework
description: A cross-industry process taxonomy. Used here for the enabling tier, where a card-specific name adds nothing: finance, HR and corporate services look much the same in any industry, and inventing local names for them costs comparability for no benefit.

name: BIAN
description: The Banking Industry Architecture Network's service landscape. A reference model of banking service domains, organized into business areas. Strong on what a bank does and deliberately silent on how it is run.
scope: Banking business capabilities and service domains

name: BIZBOK
description: The Business Architecture Guild's body of knowledge. Governs how the capability map and the value streams are built rather than what is in them, which makes it the framework this repository's own business layer answers to.

name: COBIT 2019
description: Governance and management objectives for enterprise IT. Where ITIL says how to run a service, this says how to know whether it is being run well, which is why the risk and technology governance domains answer to it.
scope: Governance and management of enterprise IT

name: CRI Profile
description: The Cyber Risk Institute's Profile: the financial sector's harmonization of NIST CSF, ISO 27001 and the regulators' expectations into one set of diagnostic statements. What a bank is examined against for cyber, and therefore what the security domain is governed by rather than informed by.
scope: Cyber risk management and resilience in financial institutions

name: DAMA-DMBOK
description: The data management body of knowledge: governance, quality, architecture, metadata, master data, security. The only one of these with a defensible account of what a data function is responsible for.

name: ISO/IEC 27001
description: The certifiable information security management standard. Named separately from the NIST framework because certification is a fact about the organization and a practice framework is not.

name: ITIL 4
description: Service management practice: incident, change, problem, service level. The frame technology operations is actually run and audited against, and the vocabulary a service management tool already speaks.

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
description: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. The five functions most security programs are structured and reported against, and the one framing a board recognizes.

name: PCI DSS
description: The card industry's data security standard. Not a framework anybody chose: it is a condition of processing card transactions, which is why it governs the payment and merchant domains whatever anyone thinks of it.

name: TOGAF
description: The architecture development method and content metamodel this repository's entity types are drawn from. It governs the practice of architecture, not any business domain, which is why nothing but the architecture function maps to it.
